title: Define settlement correction, reversal uniqueness, and control-account projections
description:
References: §§5.6/5.7, 8.1/8.2, Appendix A/B/F (lines 419-423, 519-522, 536, 1165, 1241-1246, 1335, 1339).
Open amount = original minus summed SETTLES, but no immutable application-undo law is specified when a receipt or invoice is reversed/replaced. Reversing a settled receipt's GL legs leaves the invoice closed unless settlement effects reverse too; copying the original settles into the reversal can double-apply. Define versioned application effects and their bitemporal fold, target-side/unit validation, and over-application protection.
Acyclic SUPERSEDES plus exact target negation does not prevent two different idempotency keys from reversing/replacing one original twice. O + (-O) + (-O) is still acyclic and each reversal satisfies the local rule. Specify which reversal/replacement lifecycle actions are permitted and the concurrency witness; reversing a reversal must remain explicit if supported.
§5.6 says native detail postings inherently fold into the control account. The Register key schema has one account_ref, while only Leaf accounts accept legs. Define summary roll-up ownership, prohibit double counting and specify the externally fed detail-vs-summary representation so there is no second posting universe.
Acceptance: receipt applied then reversed; invoice replaced after partial application; concurrent duplicate reversals; two customers under an AR control account plus external-summary import. W2/W3, G0/G2.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.7 application effects versioned (open = original - SETTLES + UNSETTLES; reversals carry kernel-emitted unsettles; replacements re-declare, never copy); §8.2 reversal/replacement uniqueness by identity-derived vids (second reversal = AlreadyLive conflict; reversing a reversal explicit); §5.6 leaf-only register cells with rollup cells for summaries and external detail outside the book. FA-INV-08 clauses unsettle, reversed-once. Left open for re-review.

title: fa-sim-harness: lab runtime (asupersync lab + substrate lab VFS) with registered crash points at every pipeline barrier, seeded scheduling, DPOR over post-vs-close and the other registered races, crashpacks with replay commands, in-sim consistency oracles; Genesis campaign green under lab (G1)
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): "Simulation-first (fa-sim)" is a design pillar (AGENTS.md verification ladder; plan §16) and Gate G1 requires the Genesis slice "green under lab and live". At 96d1918 there is no lab harness at all: no fa-sim-harness crate (W1 names it), no crash points, no DPOR, no crashpacks, no replay command; the only concurrency test is the policy-epoch race. The post-vs-close race that the doctrine calls "an SSI conflict, never a cron job's finding" is untested in either order. Every later workstream accrues its scenario campaigns onto this harness, so it is on the critical path to G1.

WHAT:
1. `crates/fa-sim-harness` (verification layer, test-only consumers): wraps asupersync's lab runtime (virtual time, seeded scheduling) and the substrate's lab VFS (torn writes, bit flips, ENOSPC, fsync lies) behind one `Lab { seed, schedule, vfs_faults }`; the facade `fa::Book` opens under it through the existing `Entropy::deterministic` and a lab `PurposeContexts` (no new API on Book that production code could reach).
2. Crash points at every pipeline barrier the kernel already has (admission, witnesses read, legs staged, mirrors moved, commit): a registered `CrashPoint` enum, each named in a `registries/crash_points.toml` row with the invariant it guards; the harness kills at each point and reopens; FA-INV-04/14/16 oracles (register-equals-fold, accumulator consistency, mirror-equals-payload) run after every reopen.
3. DPOR over post-vs-close, concurrent application, promotion-vs-trunk (when drafts exist), restatement-vs-reopen (when cases exist), sweep-vs-manual-void (fa-ctf): both orders explored; the winner is decided by first-committer-wins over witnesses, never by wall time.
4. Crashpacks: every failing seed writes `<scratch>/crashpacks/<seed>/` with the schedule, the VFS fault log and the exact `cargo test` replay command; the harness prints it; replay is byte-deterministic.
5. Consistency oracles as reusable in-sim checks: balance law, register-equals-fold, subledger-equals-control, admissibility at commit, SoD on approvals, idempotency stability, supersession acyclicity, accumulator consistency, bitemporal monotonicity, projection-equals-payload, erasure leaves amounts intact (those whose subsystems exist run; the rest are registered dormant with the activating bead).
6. Genesis campaign: the existing genesis/differential histories executed under the lab with 1,000 seeds and the full crash matrix; this is the G1 "green under lab" evidence.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `cargo test -p fa-sim-harness genesis_campaign` runs the matrix green and prints the seed count and crash-point coverage (every registered point hit ≥ 10 times); post-vs-close DPOR explores both orders and each ends in exactly one committed winner; [ ] planted negatives: a harness mutation that skips mirror moves on reopen fails register-equals-fold; a VFS torn-write at the commit barrier with the oracle disabled is caught by the accumulator-consistency check; [ ] proof class: bounded_model (the matrix states its bounds: seeds, depth, fault classes); [ ] consumers: Gate G1, every later campaign, fa-ctf interleavings, fa-s7x promotion races; [ ] no-claim boundary: a green campaign is bounded evidence, never a proof of crash safety beyond the registered points and seeds.

TESTS: the harness has its own unit tests for determinism (same seed → same transcript) and for crashpack replay; campaign logs record seed, point, oracle verdicts; run through rch like every other test.

title: Teller reconciliation: bank statement parsers to BankLine documents with import receipts, matching engine as adaptive decisions with decision cards and a deterministic pinned fallback, journaled Match objects with exact residual explanations, reconciliation register verified by fold with RegisterEquals attestations, three-way matching, fa bank import / fa reconcile
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Teller is bank reconciliation: bank statement parsers producing BankLine documents (W4), a matching engine whose heuristics are adaptive decisions with decision cards and a deterministic pinned fallback (AGENTS.md adaptive-decision contract), a reconciliation register and attestations. At 96d1918 there is no Teller code (2 prose hits). fa-ff6 (bank feeds through flywheel_connectors) presumes BankLine documents and the matching engine, so it depends on this bead. Reconciliation is also one of Lantern's procedures and one of the registers the plan verifies by fold.

WHAT:
1. Bank statement parsers in `fa-formats` (interop) for CSV/OFX/CAMT.053 subsets, exact amounts (fa-money), every line a content-addressed `BankLine` document (Docket) with the statement's import receipt (Docket slice 2) and `DERIVED_FROM` the statement document; fuzzed readers.
2. `crates/fa-teller` (analytics): candidate generation (amount, date window, counterparty normalization, reference tokens), scoring as an adaptive decision: the decision card records the policy epoch, state space, candidates, observed features, the expected-benefit interval and the pinned fallback (exact amount + date within N days + reference equality, deterministic tie-break by lowest entry ordinal); learned scores are advisory features only; the card never changes a committed amount.
3. Match decisions as journaled, immutable objects (`Match { bank_line_ref, entry_ref | None, decision_card_ref, principal }`), one-to-many and many-to-one with exact residual explanations (fees, FX) that must be posted as their own entries under a named law, never absorbed; unmatching is a new object with lineage.
4. The reconciliation register: per bank account × period, book balance vs statement balance with the outstanding items list as a fold of matches and bank lines; `fa verify reconciliation` refolds it; reconciliation attestations bind `cell_key + fold_digest` (RegisterEquals).
5. Three-way matching (PO/receipt/invoice) as the same engine over documents, registered as a Lantern procedure.
6. CLI: `fa bank import <file> --account <code> --json`, `fa reconcile <account> --for <period> [--dry-run] --json` (plans the matches as intents with certificates; `--yes` or confirm_plan to commit), `fa reconcile status`.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: on a fixture statement every unambiguous line matches under the pinned fallback alone (learned features disabled) and the register folds to the statement balance; replaying the decision cards reproduces every match bit-for-bit; [ ] planted negatives: a card whose fallback is removed is refused at registration; a match that would change an amount is refused; a fee residual not posted under a law leaves the register out of balance and `verify reconciliation` says so; [ ] proof class: invariant (register-equals-fold, card replay) + statistical (match quality on the labelled corpus); [ ] consumers: fa-ff6, Lantern reconciliation procedure, CPAs; [ ] no-claim boundary: a reconciled register proves matches were recorded and the fold ties, not that every match is economically correct.

TESTS: parser tests with exact-amount vectors, fa-teller unit tests on labelled corpora with per-line logs, fa-reference naive matcher differential for the fallback, CLI binary tests.

title: fa-cli: canonicalize --book / FA_BOOK before any substrate path use (a '..' component reaches fgdb-strata's and the blob store's rename, which the host VFS refuses) — planted '..' negative, byte-identical envelope for the absolute and relative spellings
description: WHY (TopazOsprey 3656, 2026-10-11, unverified observation during fa-txf t8): fa-cli's book_dir passes --book / FA_BOOK through raw. asupersync's UnixVfs::rename runs validate_safe_path (fs/path_ops.rs ~189), which refuses any '..' component, while create_dir_all and open do not validate; so a book opened as --book ../acme most likely fails at the substrate's first staging rename (fgdb-strata store.rs ~1014) or the blob store's rename, with an I/O error instead of a usable book. Agents are the primary operators and relative spellings are what they type. WHAT: (1) resolve the book directory once at the CLI boundary (fa-cli book_dir): join to the process cwd and normalize '.' and '..' lexically (no symlink resolution, no host canonicalize of a path that may not exist yet), refuse a path that escapes nothing but still carries '..' only if the normalized form cannot be produced; pass the normalized absolute path to Book::open and to the daemon request (through_daemon already prefers files.cwd); (2) the same normalization in fad's request handling so a daemon-side open sees the same path; (3) first verify the failure with a binary test (fa book create --book ../x from a temp cwd) and keep that test as the planted negative turned positive. ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: --book ../acme, --book ./acme and --book /abs/acme produce byte-identical robot envelopes (coordinate.book, data) for the same book; [ ] planted negative: before the fix the '..' spelling fails at the substrate rename (recorded in the test's doc as the observed defect), after the fix no substrate call ever sees a '..' component (a FaultVfs or path-recording VFS asserts it); [ ] proof class: invariant (one normalization point) + binary test; [ ] consumers: every agent invocation of fa with a relative --book, fad clients, the MCP posture (fa-mcp forwards cwd); [ ] no-claim boundary: this does not make the substrate tolerate '..'; it keeps such paths out of it.

title: fa-query: the FrankenAccounting GQL profile (FOR PERIOD, AS KNOWN AT, EFFECTIVE AT|BETWEEN, AT BRANCH, AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED, AS CURRENTLY STATED, AS REPORTED IN, CALL fa.*, EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)) rewritten onto substrate GQL, authorization before observation, read procedures bound to the register folds with certificates, the runtime graph (sessions, capabilities, drafts, findings, decision cards, access events) queryable read-only, fa query verb
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): The plan's query language is GQL through the substrate plus the namespaced FrankenAccounting profile (`FOR PERIOD`, `AS KNOWN AT`, `EFFECTIVE AT|BETWEEN`, `AT BRANCH`, `AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED`, `AS CURRENTLY STATED`, `AS REPORTED IN <certificate>`, `CALL fa.*`, `EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)`), and AGENTS.md requires the system's own runtime (sessions, capabilities, drafts, close runs, findings, decision cards, access events) to be a read-only, access-controlled graph queryable in GQL. At 96d1918 no GQL is executed anywhere (fgdb_gql is used once, for the symbol resolver); `fa query` does not exist. The library's `query` certified read is part of the product shape.

WHAT:
1. `crates/fa-query` (surface layer): the profile parser as a thin front that rewrites the FrankenAccounting clauses into substrate GQL with explicit known-at and effective predicates over the entry/period graph (the clauses are sugar over properties the graph already has: recorded CommitSeq, effective_date, period refs, branch id), refusing anything the profile does not name (exit 3) with the admissible form in the refusal.
2. `CALL fa.*` procedures: `fa.trial_balance`, `fa.balance`, `fa.explain_balance`, `fa.open_items`, `fa.fold` as registered read procedures bound to the same folds fa-registers uses; results carry the coordinate and a certificate when `EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)` is requested (the certificate commits to the query text, coordinate and result digest; `fa replay` re-executes).
3. Authorization precedes observation: the capability's caveats (books, accounts subtree, periods, known_at ≤ seq, branch, partial_view) are applied by refusing before query construction in the interim posture (doctrine 8), never as a result filter; whole-entry visibility rules from fa-llx apply.
4. The runtime graph: sessions, capabilities (with revocation), drafts, close runs, findings, decision cards and access events are already or become graph objects; `fa query` can read them under a capability with the `read` op and the matching scope; every read is an access event (journaled, append-only).
5. CLI/library: `Book::query(&cap, text) -> QueryResult`, `fa query "<gql>" --json`, robot events `rows`, `certificate`; byte-deterministic ordering.
6. `AS ORIGINALLY REPORTED` / `AS CURRENTLY STATED` and `AS REPORTED IN <certificate>` bind to the palimpsest registers and statement certificates when those land; until then they refuse naming their bead (never a silent fallback).

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `fa query "MATCH ... FOR PERIOD 2026-03 AS KNOWN AT 120 CALL fa.trial_balance"` returns rows equal to `fa tb --for 2026-03 --known-at 120` byte-for-byte and `EXPLAIN (CERTIFICATE)` yields a replayable certificate; a query over the runtime graph lists the caller's own session; [ ] planted negatives: a capability scoped to one account subtree refuses a query naming another before any read (no storage observation, proven by a lab VFS read counter); a clause outside the profile is refused with the admissible form; a result-filter implementation (mutation) fails the no-observation test; [ ] proof class: invariant (authorization-before-observation, FA-INV-10) + differential (query vs register folds); [ ] consumers: agents (A6), auditors pinned to a known-at, fa-mcp resources, the dogfooded runtime graph; [ ] no-claim boundary: the profile proves parity with the folds for the covered procedures, not general GQL completeness.

TESTS: parser goldens, kernel-level authorization tests with the read counter, differential vs fa-registers and fa-reference, CLI binary tests with query text and coordinate logged.

title: Period-transition control date law: derive the control's effective date from the period (close = last_day, reopen/restate = the registered boundary) instead of accepting a caller date — oracle rule, differential transition_day update, transition_proposal digest/approval/facade/CLI signature change
description: WHY (WhiteCreek 3568 (C) / RubyMoose, MistyPlateau 3574, 2026-10-11): today transition_period takes a caller-supplied effective date and copies it into the period control record; fa-registers/tests/differential.rs dates every transition 2026-01-01 (transition_day(), ~line 959; Feb/Mar/Apr transitions at ~1268) and the reference oracle admits them, so a control for March can carry Apr 15. Slice 1 of fa-llx closes the authorization hole only (the caller date joins the scoped token's footprint: its period is added to reach and through = max(period.last_day, caller date), refused in admit_within before any read). The period-law question — what date a period control legitimately carries — is a separate rule with its own oracle and differential update, and it changes transition_proposal digests, approvals and the facade/CLI signatures, so it is not a scope-slice change. WHAT: (1) decide and register the law in the plan's period section (A2) and registries/entry_classes.toml control rows: a period transition control is dated by the period it transitions (close → last_day; reopen/restate → the registered boundary), never by the caller; book-scoped controls stay undated (plan §7.1); (2) fa-reference oracle rule + fa-registers differential: drop transition_day(), derive from the period, and add a planted negative (a caller-dated transition is a usage refusal, exit 2, before any read); (3) transition_proposal: remove the date input, re-derive the digest, update approvals that bind it, the facade signature and the fa-cli verb (verbs.toml row + robot-schema fixture re-pin); (4) migration note: no users, no shim; the durable control encoding changes in place (fa-bvx owns the encoding). ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: every period control on a fresh book is dated inside its own period and the differential is green with no transition_day(); [ ] planted negative: a caller-dated transition is refused with exit 2 and an unchanged frontier; a control dated outside its period cannot be constructed (type-level) ; [ ] proof class: invariant (period law at commit) + differential; [ ] consumers: fa-llx footprint (its max(last_day, caller) term becomes last_day), fa-bvx lifecycle projections, Almanac period state machine, CLI/MCP transition verbs; [ ] no-claim boundary: this bead fixes the date law of period controls, not the admissibility matrix rows (Appendix C) themselves.

title: fa-statements report engine + Concordat: registered statement definitions, certified journal folds with replayable certificates (FA-INV-11), comparatives and restatement views, multi-book with the intercompany constraint, consolidation on drafts with journaled eliminations, revaluation/translation under registered FX laws, deterministic Markdown IR for fa-cet

WHAT:
1. `crates/fa-statements` (analytics layer): `StatementDefinition` as a registered, versioned object (registry `registries/statements/*.toml` for the standard set: balance sheet, income statement, cash flow (indirect), changes in equity, trial balance as a statement) with line items as account-subtree folds plus computed lines (arithmetic over lines, exact), sign conventions per account type, comparatives (`FOR PERIOD` vs prior), and cutoff rules from fa-xwv (special periods, carry-forward, report cutoffs).

title: Define control-record encoding and immutable lifecycle projections
description:
References: §§4.2, 5.10, 7.3, 8.3, 10.2, Appendix A/C/F (lines 286-317, 435, 483, 540, 606-620, 1144, 1200-1207, 1278-1279, 1329).
Every Entry requires 2 or more posting legs, including SchemaControl/PolicyControl/PeriodControl in the same EntryClass union. Creating the first chart/calendar/book or opening a Future period has no legitimate pair of posting legs. Encoding invented zero-value accounting legs would violate the no-prototype/no-fabricated-leg doctrine. Define a journal record union or a precisely class-dependent payload with control effects separate from posting legs.
Lifecycle objects are declared immutable after commit (FA-INV-02), yet Period.state is a versioned property, RestatementCase/CloseRun/Finding/DraftSet carry changing status, Capability carries revoked, and §5.10 compare-and-sets membership counters. Specify which immutable transition records are authoritative and which current-state objects are disposable projections, with reconstruction and known-at rules. Attestations on a Register must bind its coordinate/value digest rather than merely a mutable/rebuildable cell identity.
Negative examples: create an empty book and first account without fake legs; transition case Proposed→Approved→Posted without updating its original payload; rebuild lifecycle state from immutable transitions. W1-W4, G0.
Model follow-up: entity-scoped capabilities and cash-by-legal-entity registers require an authoritative entity assignment. Entry/Account/Leg schemas and declared edges do not identify an owning LegalEntity, and the Dimension kind list has no mandatory legal-entity dimension. title: fa-canon first slice: typed total rule language, type checker and IR, journaled content-addressed rule versions with dual-control activation, interim evaluator under a stripped Cx (no clock/entropy/net/fs, compile-fail proven), rule families bound to intents (Accrue/Defer, Allocation, Revaluation, Elimination) replacing their FA-REF-102 class refusals, golden corpora, backtesting on drafts, VM adapter boundary
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Canon (W6) is the posting-rule engine: a rule language, type checker and IR, an interim evaluator under a stripped `Cx` (no clock, entropy, network or filesystem), the intent catalog bound to rule families, golden corpora, backtesting and activation with dual control. At 96d1918 there is no Canon code at all (fa-model/src/canon.rs is the byte codec; "Canon" appears twice as forward references); Allocation/Revaluation/Elimination entry classes are refused as not implemented because no rule can produce them. Doctrine 3's sharpest instance ("a rule that wants today receives it as a declared input") has nothing to bind to. Canon depends on the intents slice (rule-driven intents are typed intents) and on W3's period law.

WHAT (first real slice):
1. `crates/fa-canon` (laws layer; pure): the rule language as a small, total, typed expression language over declared inputs (event fields, registered units, account codes, dates given as inputs), with a parser, a type checker that refuses floats and unregistered units/laws, and an IR; every rounding or allocation in a rule names a registered law from `rounding_laws.toml`.
2. Rule versions as journaled, content-addressed objects (Appendix A `RuleVersion`): source, IR digest, declared inputs, produced entry classes, activation state; activation is a PolicyControl-style control record under dual control (two distinct principals, SoD row), with `GENERATED_BY` lineage from every entry a rule produces to the rule version and `DERIVED_FROM` to the event.
3. The interim evaluator: `evaluate(rule_version, event, inputs) -> Vec<Intent>` under a stripped Cx (type-level: the evaluator's context carries no capability for clock/entropy/net/fs, proven by a compile-fail test); re-running version v over event e reproduces the entry digest (the plan's testable-derivation claim) as a test.
4. Rule families bound to intents: Accrue/Defer, Allocation (largest-remainder over a named law), Revaluation (FX law from fa-p7r), Elimination (Concordat); each family's produced class is enabled in the kernel's class gate only when its rule family exists (replacing the FA-REF-102 refusal for that class with the real path).
5. Golden corpora: checked-in events + expected intents per rule family; backtesting = replaying a rule version over a historical event range on a draft (fa-s7x) and diffing against the live entries; dry-run plans for every produced intent (fa-intents).
6. VM adapter boundary: the evaluator is behind a trait so the substrate's UDF VM (Appendix H, R-VM) can replace it with the registered switch-over rule; no substrate code copied.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: an Accrue rule produces an Adjusting intent whose entry replays byte-identically from (rule version, event); an Allocation rule's residual lands on the named rounding account under the named law; activation without a second principal is refused by SoD; [ ] planted negatives: a rule source that reads a clock-like input not declared fails type checking; a rule naming an unregistered law is refused; a mutated IR digest fails the lineage check; [ ] proof class: invariant (derivation replay) + golden corpora; [ ] consumers: Allocation/Revaluation/Elimination classes, fa-statements consolidation, agents' intent catalog; [ ] no-claim boundary: Canon proves rules are deterministic and typed, not that any rule encodes the right accounting policy.

TESTS: fa-canon unit tests for parser/type checker/IR with goldens, kernel tests for lineage and activation SoD, differential vs a fa-reference naive evaluator for the first families, logs naming the rule version digest.

description:

- §4.7 and FA-REF-015 refuse instants as effective dates, while §15.3 silently converts with a warning. Pick one explicit policy. Period inadmissibility is exit 2 in Genesis but listed under exit 7 too.
- CLI fa hold is both financial hold and governance hold place/release; MCP catalog has no complete governance/registry/interop/lifecycle mapping despite parity claim. Declare unambiguous verbs and shared-operation mappings or registered exclusions.
- Closed/Locked matrix permits Resolution(Voids), Revision and Reopen, but §7.3/FA-INV-03 says only restatement classes; matrix requires post_softclosed, migrate, schema_change absent from the §14.2 closed op vocabulary. Reconcile from one registry.
- Bundles claim same scope+checkpoint yields same bytes but include producer, produced_at_seq, capability and redaction fields; bind the complete closure or split deterministic content from production receipt. Fixed-as_known_at RegisterEquals assertions cannot become false from later entries; use a separate head-following reconciliation monitor and retain the original assertion.
- §15.5 example needs IS edges, Subledger→Account CONTROLS, LegalEntity.code and Leg.effective_date not declared in the model. Fix the model/query contract and reject cross-unit sums in the accounting GQL profile.
- fa-formats/qbo and object_schemas/tracing/conversion laws need explicit registry ownership; ftui and fsci_stats are promised despite the closed four-foundation policy. Reconcile their inclusion/exclusion with explicit posture/test-only policy, never silent allowlist expansion.
- Plan/README characterize all ERP posted journals as editable rows. Oracle Fusion documentation explicitly says a posted journal cannot be changed and describes reversal workflows: https://docs.oracle.com/cloud/131/user_services/FAFTT/F416502AN10266.htm . Narrow competitive claims and separate existing derived balance caches from authoritative mutable accounting facts. SEC audit-trail amendments were adopted October 12, 2022, not 2023 as §0 says: https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2022-187 .

title: Specify N-leg hold resolution, reserved availability, and expiry-period behavior
description:
References: §§5.4/5.5, 7.6, Appendix A/B/C/F/G (lines 409-415, 495, 1175, 1242, 1268, 1342, 1374).
Posts { amount: Amount } generalizes a two-leg TigerBeetle transfer inadequately to N-leg/multi-unit holds. A pending USD entry D A60, D B40, C cash100 resolved for 60 admits D A60/C cash60 or D A20/D B40/C cash60, both balanced and under original legs. Neither schema nor law chooses. Multiple currencies cannot fit one Amount. Require a per-leg balanced subvector, named proportional law, or explicit registered absence.
Limit reads say head net balance but do not define worst-case reserved availability. With cash100, a pending outflow80 must block a second80 and an unrelated posted outflow30; pending inflow cannot finance an outflow before resolution. Specify reserve/consume/release equations and atomic witnesses.
Pending created in Open can encounter Closed/Locked before timeout. Appendix C allows only Voids in Locked, excluding Expires; §5.4 requires Expires for every elapsed deadline, so the sweep can become permanently inadmissible. Define origin-vs-posting-period routing, unconditional lawful reservation release, and close/lock preconditions.
A bounded sweep cannot both expire every due hold in one transaction and obey max_batch_entries for an arbitrarily large due population. Pin epoch/cursor/batch progression and visibility under backlog. Apply the same precision to scheduled reversals after the target period closes.
Acceptance: the N-leg ambiguity above; multi-unit partial; pending-spend race; locked-period expiration; sweep batch overflow; crash/manual-resolution interleavings. W2/W3, G0/G2.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.4 Posts{posted_legs} per-leg balanced sub-vector (scalar = two-leg sugar; ProportionalPost law), resolution unique by identity-derived vid (manual void vs sweep = AlreadyLive conflict), timeout measured from the TimeEvidence tick, reserved-availability equations (pending outflows reserve, pending inflows never finance), SweepCursor batching under max_batch_entries; Appendix C Pending/Resolution rows (Voids/Expires admissible except Future); Appendix A Disposition; Appendix B PostReserve. title: fad tick/sweep scheduler and CLI timing intents: the clock and the System authority live in fad only (plan §5.4; no fa tick/sweep, no --grant system in the embedded CLI)
description:
WHY (CobaltGull ruling 2026-10-11 01:3xZ on JadePeak 3346): plan §5.4 says "the fa daemon orders one ExpirySweep control entry per configured tick carrying rollback-resistant time evidence". The kernel side is landed (fa-ctf: record_tick with TickRequest, sweep/sweep_batch under the book's System principal, due_holds/due_reversals, scheduled reversals by identity) but nothing drives it: fa post still refuses timeout_ns, with_auto_reverse has no CLI, and no posture records ticks. Doctrine 3 and 6 fix where the clock may live: a posting rule never reads the wall clock, recorded time is never user-supplied, and the lab runtime's virtual clock is the only legitimate control of the ticks. The embedded `fa` CLI therefore never reads a clock and never mints System authority; fad, as the posture that owns the writer lease, does both.

WHAT:
1. fad scheduler: a `[daemon] tick_ns` row in registries/verbs.toml; fad reads its own clock under its Cx (clock capability granted to fad only), records one TimeEvidence tick per interval through `Book::record_tick(observed_utc_ns, capability)` with the System capability it derives from the book's keys as lease holder, then runs one bounded sweep (`Book::sweep(capability, max_batch)`) and one bounded scheduled-reversal batch; `fad sweep-now` for an operator-requested cycle; every cycle is journaled as the existing control records, nothing else.
2. Book adapters (fa crate): record_tick / sweep / sweep_reversals taking the capability; the principal is the capability's holder, which the kernel requires to be System; describe = seal_text, fallible (KernelError::Entropy propagates, txn.abort() first, per 3303/3304); no principal argument from the caller; never mint System in an adapter.
3. fa CLI: post intents gain `timeout_ns` (Pending) and `reverse_on` (Adjusting) as data only; `fa triage` reports due_holds / due_reversals / blocked_reversals and names the next step ("start fad serve --book <dir>; it ticks and sweeps"); there is NO `fa tick`, NO `fa sweep`, and NO `--grant system` in the embedded CLI (an ambient-authority escape hatch, refused by design).
4. Refusals: a sweep request without the System capability is the existing 013; a tick with a non-monotonic observation follows the registered tick law (094–098); a daemon without a clock capability refuses to start its scheduler with a typed error naming the posture.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: under the lab runtime's virtual time a Pending with timeout_ns expires on the first tick past its deadline via fad's scheduler and `fa triage` then reports zero due; an Adjusting with reverse_on is reversed by the scheduled batch at the period open; a `fad sweep-now` sweeps exactly the due population under max_batch_entries; [ ] planted negatives: the embedded CLI has no verb that records a tick (parity test over verbs.toml); an adapter that accepts a caller-supplied principal fails the kernel's System check (013); an entropy failure in describe aborts the transaction and leaves frontier, cursor, resolution and reversal unchanged, then a retry succeeds; a wall-clock read anywhere outside fad's scheduler fails the Cx capability audit; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-15.expiry live, recorded-time-never-user-supplied) + lab-runtime simulation; [ ] consumers: operators running fad, agents reading triage, G2; [ ] no-claim boundary: virtual-time proofs show the scheduler's law, not wall-clock accuracy of a production host.

TESTS: fad lab tests under virtual time (tick → expiry → triage zero; scheduled reversal at open; sweep-now bounded), fa-cli binary tests for the new intent fields and triage lines with transcripts logged, parity test that verbs.toml has no tick/sweep verb for the embedded posture, Cx capability audit test.

title: Close evidence-required and retention/erasure contract gaps
description:
References: §§8.5, 9.1/9.2/9.6, 10.2, 14.6, Appendix A/B/F (lines 548, 560-564, 580, 618, 795, 1152-1153, 1188-1194, 1232, 1254, 1332).
Common intent evidence is optional and Entry.evidence has no minimum or class-specific source contract. A registered Intent origin with an empty evidence list satisfies the written unknown-reference check vacuously, contrary to AGENTS' rule that an entry without registered evidence is unencodable. Define required real evidence by class (manual assertion/control authority may be explicit objects), and distinguish drafts from committable entries.
External documents retain locator+observed digest, not necessarily bytes. FA-INV-05 promises strong retention of the provenance closure for the retention floor. Specify durable custody requirements or a downgraded, non-equivalent external-evidence profile with failure behavior; a URL alone cannot ensure retention.
AttachEvidence appends edges after commit but Entry.evidence is digest-covered and immutable. Separate original posting evidence from later supplemental evidence, version the latter and specify how each closure is selected/certified.
Erasure promises no PII outside Party/Document, but immutable descriptions, leg memos, tags, external IDs, source-entered-by fields and structured event data can carry PII. Specify schema-level sensitive-field placement and key granularity; erasing a Party alone cannot remove those copies. Add live foundation ledger rows for erasure/retention/legal-hold capabilities rather than assuming them.
Acceptance: absent required evidence, lost external source, supplemental document after posting, PII in each allowed free-text location, legal hold vs erasure race, preservation of public amount commitments. W2/W4/Steward, G0.
Resolve provenance edge retention types too: bare substrate Oid/MarkerRef are identities, not retention edges. Appendix A imports a typed-reference law but uses bare Oids widely; enumerate strong/weak/cut-conditioned references and their erasure interaction so FA-INV-05 is actually enforceable.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §9.2 evidence_policy.toml minimums per class (ManualAssertion with reason code as the honest alternative; NeedsEvidence drafts cannot promote), external evidence retains bytes by default with an attested ByReferenceOnly downgrade, SupplementalEvidence as a new object; §8.5 Erasable<T> fields (description, memo, tags, external ids, migration names, event attributes) under per-Party subject keys, hold/erasure race as a witness conflict; Appendix A reference law (strong/weak/locator) and Erasable schema; Appendix H R-ERASE/R-RED/R-KEY; FA-INV-05 clauses. Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: Erasable review (WhiteCreek 2751/2756) accepted: deterministic sealing withdrawn before any commit; randomized salt+nonce from the facade's CryptoCx; AAD binds field_digest + subject_ref; retry equivalence = EntryPayload::semantic_digest under the key (in-memory normal form, never stored); FA-REF-033 when a sealed field cannot be opened; CLI intent_oid is a domain-separated BLAKE3 over (book, principal, key), never raw request bytes. Open question flagged to reviewers: proposal_digest covers full Erasable wire bytes (code) vs field_digest-only (prose).
2026-10-10 CobaltGull (WhiteCreek 2781 obligations, recorded): (1) authenticated requester binding must precede both the exact-digest and semantic retry paths — in the embedded posture the facade caller is the trusted process and proposal.principal_ref is its claim; the daemon/MCP posture must bind the principal from the session before calling post (lands with Steward, fa-llx); (2) the semantic transcript now carries each erasable field's subject_ref ahead of its plaintext, so distinct subject contexts never compare equal; (3) PostRequest no longer carries a separate principal_scope — identity scope is derived from proposal.principal_ref, and the base  capability is checked before any storage observation (doctrine 8). Remaining: caller-authenticated use is unsupported until Steward; documented on post().

title: Preserve publication and historical identity in migration and scenario interim postures
description:
References: §§5.8, 8.6, 15.2, Appendix G/H (lines 427, 552, 833-835, 1371, 1376, 1395, 1402).
§5.8 promises staging followed by one atomic migration finalization. R-BULK's interim is ordinary committed WriteBatch chunks with manifests/resume; no staging visibility or finalization filter is defined. Readers may see an incomplete migration, and a later bad chunk cannot roll back already committed entries. Specify durable staging within the same engine, activation semantics and failure/retry visibility, without deleting history.
Scenario fallback replays trunk into a fresh open_memory database, whose assigned CommitSeq/HLC and allocated VIds differ. Entry digests embed book/branch/account identities, and approvals/certificates bind those digests. Pin original-coordinate provenance and identity translation or a read-only base-plus-overlay abstraction so replay does not forge recorded time or claim original membership. Replaying only accounting objects cannot reproduce physical sequences containing access logs/checkpoints/maintenance.
Close rehearsal needs computable draft balances before substrate branches exist, but §15.2 describes draft materialization as future optional and scratch replay only for scenarios. State the shared law for all draft report reads and for promotion changing head.
Restatement case posting is atomic in §8.3/§5.1 yet Appendix G allows a separate case-transition transaction. Place the entries and posted-state effect in one transaction or specify exact recoverable state and idempotency preventing repost.
Acceptance: invalid final migration chunk, crash around activation; scratch replay with intervening system records; draft-to-trunk digest/approval changes; crash after case entries before transition. W2-W4/W5, G0/G2.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §8.6 MigrationRun staging invisible until Finalize (Abandoned runs stay journaled and invisible; retries are new runs); §15.2 one scratch-book law for drafts and scenarios (accounting objects only, identity-derived vids and seq-free payloads preserve digests and approvals, SeqMap in the certificate, no forged membership); Appendix G restatement case post is one write_ordered transaction with its LifecycleTransition. Left open for re-review.

Distinguish no engine dependency from no foundation dependency; independently verify arithmetic rather than allowing shared bugs to make differential green.
- README's G1 demo command requires fa-gen to be shipped, while fa-gen is a test-only verification crate outside every posture closure. Assign production-safe demo generation explicitly without linking the reference oracle.
Acceptance: machine-readable acyclic crate graph and work graph; each Genesis behavior maps to a live prerequisite checker; sim available before first Folio line; reference allowlist consistent with transitive closures. W1-W10, G0/G1.

title: Make unit evolution, signs, overflow, and FX residual laws mutually consistent
description:
References: §§4.4, 5.2, 6.1/6.4/6.7, Appendix A/F (lines 325, 395, 443, 455, 467, 1131-1132, 1145-1146, 1328, 1333).
1. Amount stores only unit_id and i128 mantissa. §4.4 allows changing that unit's scale and rescaling every stored mantissa, contradicting immutable entries and digests. Example: mantissa 100 means 1 at scale 2 and 0.1 at scale 3. Use immutable unit-version identity with a named conversion/migration law; never silently reinterpret or rewrite historical payloads. Distinguish precision changes from economic redenomination.
2. Entry legs have both Debit/Credit and signed i128 without a nonnegative-leg rule. Reversal wording says exact negation without deciding side swap vs signed storno. Negative legs can undermine per-side amount limits and produce two representations of the same posting. Define one canonical sign convention and boundary behavior, including i128::MIN.
3. Bounded checked i128 amounts are not an unrestricted ordered abelian group: MAX+1 and -MIN fail. Proofs/metamorphics need representability hypotheses or an unbounded reference domain; summation policy must define intermediate overflow and register cumulative totals.
4. FX residual encoding is incomplete: EUR debit 1 minor unit + debit 1 = credit 2; at rate 1/2 under HalfUp, USD base debits 1+1 != credit 1. Adding one USD credit residual fixes base balance but violates USD per-unit balance. Define lawful base-only valuation/residual effects or a complete balanced construction, including remeasurement and historical-cost release, without inventing funds or weakening FA-INV-01.
Acceptance must include these exact examples, inverse/cross-rate scale boundaries, negative refunds/allocations and both per-unit/base validation. W1/W2/W7, G0.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.4 immutable unit versions (USD@2 -> USD@4 via ScaleConversion law + Redenomination record; historical mantissas never reinterpreted), non-negative mantissas with side swap (no storno; i128::MIN unreachable), bounded register accumulators; §6.1 bounded abelian group with representability hypothesis and independent reference arithmetic; §5.2 valuation residual absorbed by a designated leg with the exact EUR 0.01+0.01/0.02 @ 1/2 HalfUp counterexample, conversion-account pairing for realized FX, revaluation through Valuation contra leaves; §6.5 lot laws. Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: fa-money valuation test realizes the EUR 0.01+0.01/0.02 @ ½ HalfUp counterexample (designated-leg residual). title: Evidence and memo full-text search via frankensearch Quill (native pure-Rust BM25, FSLX segments, delta-visible indexing) over Documents' derived text, entry descriptions and memos — pinned by git rev, default features only (no tantivy lane)
description:
WHY: investigators and agents need full-text search over evidence documents (derived text from fa-646), entry descriptions, memos and findings; the substrate's Beacon indexes cover structural lookups, not ranked text retrieval. The owner's frankensearch (/data/projects/frankensearch, last commit 2026-10-10) ships Quill (crates/frankensearch-quill v0.4.0): a native pure-Rust BM25 lexical engine with FSLX segments and delta-visible indexing, receipted at ~0.2 ms lexical search over 1K docs; tantivy remains only as an opt-in conformance oracle lane (features lexical-tantivy / tantivy-oracle) outside Quill's dependency graph, and frankensearch-fsfs's pdf-extract path is not needed. Owner correction 2026-10-10 overrides the survey's earlier not-applicable verdict.
WHAT: depends on fa-lp6 (Documents) and fa-646 (derived text). (1) pin frankensearch-quill (and only the crates it needs) by git rev with default features; record the closure in deny.toml; (2) a derived, rebuildable index over Documents' text layers, entry descriptions (opened under the book key — the index lives next to the book, never in a bundle, and is erased with the subject key per the erasure contract) and findings; the index is a register in the doctrine sense: never authoritative, rebuilt from the journal, verified by fa verify search (document set hash vs index manifest); (3) fa search <query> [--kind document|entry|finding] --json with ranked results carrying the Document oid / entry vid and the snippet, exit 0 on empty results; (4) the semantic (embedding) tiers are NOT adopted in this slice (model downloads, f32 scores) — lexical only; revisit for the two-tier mode later with an explicit decision.
ACCEPTANCE: [ ] index rebuild is deterministic for the same document set (manifest digest pinned in a test); [ ] erasure of a subject key removes its text from the index (test); [ ] fa search binary test over a fixture book; [ ] no amounts are parsed from search results; [ ] search never reads the wall clock. UPSTREAM: none required; optional issue: a minimal frankensearch-quill feature set for library consumers without the storage/ops crates.

title: Steward authority model from franken_alignment: one-shot permits bound to an immutable payload (confirm_plan), conserved rights (ceilings/escrow), dominator/min-cut separation-of-duties proofs over the authority graph, judgment caching with emptiness witnesses — invariants ported as fa-policy tests now, protocol connection later
description:
WHY: fa-llx (fa-policy) is open and the owner's franken_alignment (GitHub Dicklesworthstone/franken_alignment; reference model; zero external crates; nightly-2026-09-07) already formalises exactly the semantics the plan wants for Steward: permits bound to an unchangeable payload (= plan → commit with confirm_plan), conserved rights where held + available + spent == total (= capability ceilings via UsageCell and fa-escrow), authority-graph dominators and minimum cuts proving every path from an Agent principal to `post`/`period close` passes an approval node (SoD, computable with fnx), judgment caching with 'this range is empty' witnesses (= PlanInvalidated), DecisionClosure (= certificate).
WHAT: depends on fa-llx. (1) Port the invariants as fa-policy property tests (conservation, permit single-use, SoD dominator property) before the policy crate grows; (2) model the authority graph in the runtime graph (principals, capabilities, approvals as vertices/edges) and compute the dominator/min-cut SoD proof with fnx as a certified read; (3) later: connect FA write verbs as effects behind franken_alignment's effect gate with FA certificates/refusals as the permit evidence — blocked today by crate-name collisions (it also names fa-reference, fa-policy, fa-verify, fa, fa-cli → `package =` renames) and the newer nightly.
ACCEPTANCE: [ ] property tests for conservation and single-use permits; [ ] SoD proof over a fixture authority graph with a planted bypass path detected; [ ] no new dependency until the collision/nightly issues are resolved upstream (GH issue filed). NON-GOALS: linking franken_alignment in this slice.

title: Drafts and promotion (A6, doctrine 10 interim posture): intent-log drafts, Agent-profile work lands on a draft, authorized promotion replays to trunk
description:
Background: plan bet A6 says agents work on drafts that cannot touch trunk without authorized promotion; doctrine 10 names the interim posture while substrate branches are not live: intent-log drafts (a DraftSet lifecycle object whose body is the ordered list of intents/proposals, journaled; nothing in it is a trunk entry). fa-llx (MistyPlateau, 2026-10-10) ships the Agent-profile trunk refusal FA-REF-013 whose fix text must cite this bead because the draft path does not exist yet.

Scope: (1) DraftSet lifecycle object (Appendix A): immutable body = book, branch-or-interim marker, owner principal, ordered intents with their dry-run plan certificates and proposal_digests; status projection by LifecycleTransition control entries (Open -> Submitted -> Promoted|Rejected|Abandoned). (2) fa draft new|add|show|submit|promote|abandon with --json and robot envelope events; Agent-profile capabilities may create/add/submit, never promote. (3) Promotion = an authorized Human/System principal replays every intent against trunk inside the normal posting kernel (period law, admissibility, SoD, evidence minimum all re-evaluated at promotion time); any intent whose proposal_digest differs from the draft's recorded digest (because trunk moved: period closed, chart changed, policy epoch changed) is refused with a typed refusal naming the drift, never silently re-approved (FA-INV-10 approval-binds-proposal). (4) Metamorphic test: draft promotion == trunk post (same entries, same digests, same register cells) for model-generated histories; property: a rejected/abandoned draft leaves trunk byte-identical. (5) Oracle: fa-reference models a draft as a list of intents replayed through its own post; differential with planted negatives: Agent promoting (refused), promotion after period close (refused per matrix), drift in proposal_digest (refused), valid promotion (admitted). (6) Switch-over rule registered: when substrate branches land, DraftSet body gains a branch id and promotion becomes a branch merge; the intent-log remains the lineage.

No-claim boundary: green proves promotion re-runs the kernel and refuses drift; it does not prove agents cannot post to trunk through some other surface (that is fa-llx's FA-REF-013 and its tests).

Tests with detailed logging: kernel tests in crates/fa-journal/tests, CLI binary tests, differential floors for each planted negative.

title: Specify public evidence commitments and scope-completeness proofs
description:
References: §§9.1/9.6, 11.11, 13.1-13.3, 15.6, Appendix A/F (lines 560, 580, 704, 745-755, 917, 1188-1194, 1217-1223, 1341).
The MMR is ordered by commit, whereas bundle scopes filter by effective period/account subtree, and retroactive entries make matching records noncontiguous. Inclusion proofs prove supplied leaves belong; they do not prove all matching leaves were supplied. Appendix A contains inclusion_paths but no range/selection-completeness proof, while the CPA workflow says fa-verify confirms a complete FY extract. A producer can omit one matching entry and all retained membership proofs still verify.
Define a sound supported proof mode (e.g. verify the full relevant prefix and selection or an authenticated predicate index bound to the same checkpoint), exact scope/known-at/auth intersection, missing-entry negative vectors, and accurate costs. Do not label membership_only as complete.
Document Oid uses the substrate's keyed identity (fgdb-crypto/src/lib.rs:80-97). A verifier with only public bundle/root cannot recompute it without K_oid. ImportReceipt.digest_at_receipt could provide a public binding, but its algorithm/domain and authenticated binding to Document Oid, kind, bytes and length are not specified. Require an explicit public body commitment chain without disclosing the storage key.
Whole-document hash alone also cannot verify arbitrary disclosed byte ranges against the original redacted document. Define chunk commitments or weaken the redaction proof scope honestly. Specify signature schemes, public trust anchors, key rotation and signed transcript; the std-only verifier budget must cover these implementations.
RFC scope reference: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9162.html . W4/W9, G0/G1.
The canonical Entry deliberately excludes its creating MarkerRef/recorded time. An MMR leaf of only Entry bytes plus a checkpoint's aggregate commit_seq does not authenticate the per-entry commit sequence/HLC, especially when one commit has many leaves. Specify a domain-separated leaf envelope binding record kind, book/branch, creating marker/sequence, and within-commit ordinal, with canonical ordering and a proof of the sequence-to-prefix boundary used by historical selection.
notes: Addressed in ff3b6eb: §13.2 LeafEnvelope binding kind/coordinate/commit_seq/within-commit ordinal/selection fields; ScopeIndexComplete mode with scope_index_root in every checkpoint and boundary-neighbor proofs (missing-entry negative vectors); §9.1 public doc_commit over a 4 KiB chunk tree (substrate ObjectId is a locator only), redaction at chunk granularity labeled honestly; Ed25519 + TrustAnchorSet + KeyRotation in the std-only verifier budget; §13.1 completeness_scope labels; Appendix A LeafEnvelope/ScopeIndex/TransparencyCheckpoint/Bundle; FA-INV-14 clauses. Left open for re-review.

title: Remove approval and certificate hash cycles before freezing durable schemas
description:
References: §4.2/4.6, §10.1/10.4, Appendix A (plan lines 294-305, 333, 592, 645, 1128-1172, 1200-1223).
Entry BodyDigest excludes only entry_digest and includes approvals. ApprovalRef itself contains approved_digest. §4.6 requires that digest to equal the committed object's digest. Consequently d = H(entry containing approval.approved_digest = d), a cryptographic fixed point rather than a constructible approval flow. RestatementCase similarly embeds approvals and mutable lifecycle status. Attestation and checkpoint signature transcripts also lack explicit exclusions of the signatures and signed-digest fields.
Certificate/output references have a related missing contract: Finding contains certificate_oid and the certificate contains output_digest of the result; bundles contain report certificates; Origin::Intent contains plan_certificate_oid. Without a distinct semantic output body, hashing can become cyclic or depend on runtime IDs/approvals and make Canon's byte-for-byte replay claim impossible.
Required repair: an explicit acyclic identity/transcript graph separating immutable proposal digest, approvals/signatures, committed envelope digest, and certified semantic output. Bind approvals to complete effects, book, target coordinate and policy epoch; require reapproval if promotion replays materially different effects. Enumerate ordered construction and digest tags for every signed/certified type. Negative acceptance: change one leg after approval must fail, while adding the first valid approval must be constructible without finding a hash fixed point. W1/W3/W4, G0.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §4.6 acyclic identity graph (EntryProposal -> proposal_digest -> plan certificate -> Approvals binding proposal_digest+effects_digest+coordinate+policy epoch -> envelope entry_digest); Appendix A Entry/Approval/Attestation/Checkpoint transcripts exclude signatures/self-digests; normative construction order added; RestatementCase split into immutable body + projection with Approval objects; negative acceptance stated (leg change after approval => digest mismatch refusal; first approval needs no fixed point). Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: code consequences landed in fa-model/fa-journal: (1) plan_certificate_oid moved out of the proposal into the envelope (entry_digest = H(domain ‖ proposal_digest ‖ opt(plan_cert) ‖ approvals)); test envelope_fields_change_the_entry_digest_but_not_the_proposal_digest. (2) Idempotency: same key + different content refuses FA-REF-032 exit 6 on both the retry and race-recovery paths (RubyMoose 2739 / WhiteCreek 2730); tests identical_retry_is_recorded_and_a_changed_retry_is_a_conflict + CLI test. (3) Erasable sealing is deterministic under the key (salt/nonce KDF-derived) so identical retries compare equal; WhiteCreek carries the Appendix A row in their patch. (4) fa:entry:v1 is positional schema 1.0: the first additive field needs a minor bump + length-delimited extension block (WhiteCreek 2734) — not yet implemented; lands with the first schema patch that needs it.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: schema-review.patch (RubyMoose/WhiteCreek) APPLIED to the plan text; code parity, row by row — NOT YET ADMITTED by fa:entry:v1 as encoded: effective_date: Option<DateDay> (code: DateDay on every entry incl. controls); Disposition::Posts { source_ordinals } (code: posted_legs); settles.target_leg: EntryTarget (code: EntryRef); ControlPayload::ReservationRelease (absent); ProposalRef/EffectManifest/IntentOutcome objects (absent; no vid(IntentOutcome) yet, refusals are not durable); Certificate resolved_sequence/resolution_frontier/instant_resolution and DocumentStub proof grammar (no certificate/document code yet). ADMITTED: FA-INV-09 semantic-request equivalence (EntryPayload::semantic_digest, FA-REF-032/033). Each row lands with its slice via the minor-version + extension-block mechanism (msg 2734); the live codec is positional schema 1.0.

title: Bind commit authorization and audit delivery to explicit current policy
description:
References: §§5.1/5.10, 9.7, 14.2-14.4, Appendix A/G/H (lines 375-386, 435, 584, 779-787, 1224-1225, 1365-1375, 1399).
Plan has initial admission and commit-time SoD but no explicit current-policy witness for revocation/expiry between dry run and commit, or for reads pinned before revocation. known_at should select accounting history without resurrecting revoked access. Define security epoch, current authority evaluation, approval authority expiry/revocation policy and fail-closed boundaries.
daily_total and per-entry amount ceilings require a precise measure (gross debit, credit, absolute per-leg, per-unit), day/time-zone source, shared principal/token scope and serializable budget debit. Net of balanced entries is always zero. Attenuation/issuance must not reset a principal ceiling. No operation-cost row prices those stateful checks.
Every external-profile read must be completely logged, but Appendix G declares balance/report/bundle reads 0 writes. Define durable access recording before protected bytes escape, stream/cancellation/failure semantics, daemon authority for read-only callers, and avoidance of recursive log reads. Price the real transaction/barrier or name a distinct admitted audit path.
Account-subtree/dimension caveats and full immutable Entry payloads conflict when one entry crosses an authorized and unauthorized account: define whole-entry admission, redacted/partial-view representation and proof scope, or refuse before fetching; do not return the full other-account leg or silently describe a partial fold as whole-book.
Acceptance: revoke after plan, historical read using revoked token, two simultaneous daily-budget posts, token attenuation, crash before/after first protected output byte, and split-scope balanced entry. W2/Steward/W5, G0/G1.
The ordering of ADMIT→RESOLVE→CANON also needs explicit post-evaluation authorization: a typed event does not yet have its generated accounts/dimensions/amounts at step 1. Safely admit explicit inputs, run under restricted capabilities, then validate every generated effect and current caveat before commit. Initial authorization of the verb alone is insufficient.
notes:
Addressed in ff3b6eb: §5.1 step 5 post-evaluation authorization of rule-generated legs; §14.2 closed ops vocabulary, current-policy witness at commit (PlanInvalidated{CapabilityRevoked}), historical selectors never resurrect authority, ceiling measure (per-leg mantissa; daily gross debits per root issuance; day from TimeEvidence) via a UsageCell, whole-entry visibility with partial_view; §9.7 AccessEvent committed before the first protected byte and priced as an Appendix G row; FA-INV-10 clauses. Left open for re-review.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: capability checks in the Genesis slice are caller-supplied ops (Capability::with_ops) evaluated before observation for the base  op and inside the transaction for matrix ops; there is no authenticated principal binding yet (WhiteCreek 2781) — Steward (fa-llx) must bind principal + capability from an authenticated session before the kernel is reached, and the daemon must refuse caller-asserted principals.
2026-10-10 CobaltGull: correction — the previous note lost a word to shell expansion: the base "post" op is checked before observation; matrix ops are checked inside the transaction.

title: Docket slice 2: custody chains, ImportRun control records with receipt hashes, external document storage behind public commitments with verified reads, redaction contracts as derived objects, retention holds blocking erasure and expiry
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Docket's first slice (fa-lp6) delivers content-addressed documents, chunk-Merkle commitments, evidence minimums and `EVIDENCED_BY`; fa-journal/src/evidence.rs lists custody, import receipts, bank lines, external storage and redaction as "later slices". Plan §9 and W4 require them before Gate G2 ("documents, custody, attestations, balance assertions"). fa-v74 (subject keys) and fa-646 (intake pipeline) touch adjacent ground; fa-j9t is the spec-side contract bead. This bead is the code.

WHAT:
1. Custody chain: every document carries an immutable `Custody` lineage (received-from principal/system, received-at CommitSeq, transfer events as journaled objects), queryable as `fa document custody <oid>`; a document cannot be cited by an entry unless its custody chain is complete to a registered intake source.
2. Import receipts: `ImportRun` as a control record (legs = []) with the source descriptor, byte count, document count, the Merkle root over the imported documents' oids, and a receipt hash the external party can keep; `fa import receipt <run>`; receipts are what fa-ff6 and fa-646 must produce.
3. External document storage: documents above the inline threshold store bytes outside the journal under a registered store descriptor with the public commitment (chunk-tree root) inline; reads verify the commitment on every access; a missing external blob is a typed refusal (exit 5, foundation/I-O) and never a silent null; the plan's "public commitments" let a bundle prove a document without shipping it.
4. Redaction contracts: `redaction = <contract>` capability caveat; a redacted view of a document is a derived object with its own commitment and lineage to the original; redaction never changes an amount or an entry (erasure-leaves-amounts-intact oracle); subject-key erasure (fa-v74) composes with this.
5. Retention holds: `RetentionHold` control records that block erasure cuts and expiry sweeps for the held subjects; releases are journaled.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: an import run of N documents produces a receipt whose root recomputes from the oids; an external document reads back byte-identically with the commitment verified; a redacted view omits the field and keeps the entry's amounts; a hold blocks an erasure cut with a refusal naming the hold; [ ] planted negatives: a tampered external blob is refused on read (exit 8); a document without custody cannot be cited (refusal names the missing link); an erasure cut under a hold is refused; [ ] proof class: invariant (commitments, lineage) + differential (fa-reference naive custody/receipt model); [ ] consumers: fa-ff6, fa-646, fa-v74, bundles (A3), G2; [ ] no-claim boundary: receipts prove what was imported, not that the source was truthful.

TESTS: kernel tests in fa-journal/tests with oids and roots logged, CLI binary tests, differential floors per planted negative.

title: Subject keys: per-Party erasable-field keys held outside the journal (R-KEY), managed by fad, with Party objects; ErasureCut switch-over from the typed refusal
description:
Background: fa-lp6 (TopazOsprey, 2026-10-10) ships Erasable<T> fields with subject_ref but every key is the book key, and ErasureCut is a typed refusal (FA-REF-088) citing plan 8.5 / Appendix H R-ERASE: an FA-level tombstone that leaves plaintext reachable is a prohibited shortcut, so erasure waits for destroyable per-subject keys. The invariant 'redaction or key loss never changes an amount' is proven in fa-lp6 on the real substrate.

Scope: (1) Party objects (vertices, content-addressed, immutable body) as the subjects of erasable fields; (2) a subject-key store OUTSIDE the append-only journal: a keys file owned by fad (writer lease) with per-Party keys, key ids referenced from Erasable<T>.subject_ref, key creation journaled as a control entry naming the key id (never the key), destruction journaled as a typed tombstone naming the key id and the legal basis; (3) fold/read behaviour with a destroyed key: amounts, digests, registers, trial balance unchanged; erased fields render as a typed absence naming the tombstone; retry equivalence per FA-REF-033; (4) ErasureCut control entry (plan 8.5) admitted only with a destroyable key present, SoD row for erasure, refusal rows updated; (5) oracle in fa-reference models key presence; differential plants: erasure with the book key (refused), erasure of a subject with live legal hold (refused), valid erasure (admitted, amounts unchanged), read after destruction (typed absence); (6) CLI: fa party add, fa erase <subject> --basis <code> --yes, fa keys status; MCP parity later.

Depends on fa-lp6 (Erasable fields, SupplementalEvidence) and fa-i8j (fad owns the keys file). No-claim boundary: green proves key destruction removes plaintext reachability through FA's own readers and never changes an amount; it does not claim substrate-level erasure (R-ERASE) or storage-media guarantees.

Testing: real-substrate kernel tests, CLI binary tests with detailed logs, differential floors for each planted negative.

title: fa-registers maintainer: incremental delta_since folds with a CAS watermark, RegisterCheckpoint control records with checkpoint cadence as a decision card, rebuild = maintained metamorphic, recovery discards and rebuilds, read paths never serve stale cells, Ripple switch-over rule registered
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Bet A1 says balances are "materialized incrementally and verifiable by recomputation", W2 names "the fa-registers maintainer over delta_since", and Appendix H registers the interim posture for Ripple views as a FrankenAccounting-level `delta_since` register maintainer. At 96d1918 every fold is a full rescan of the entry stream at a known-at seq (fa-registers/src/lib.rs `fold_period`, `trial_balance_at`); `materialize` writes register vertices and `verify_period` compares, but there is no incremental maintainer, no watermark advance from `delta_since`, no checkpoints, and `delta_since` has 0 hits. This is correct but will not scale, and the recovery rule ("recovery discards and rebuilds") has no code path to exercise.

WHAT:
1. The maintainer: `Registers::advance(&cx, book)` reads the substrate's `delta_since(watermark)` entry stream, folds only the new entries into the register cells (period × account × unit, plus the pending, open-item, availability and per-entity cells as they exist), moves the watermark under CAS inside the same transaction, and is idempotent under crash (re-running from a stale watermark yields identical cells).
2. Checkpoints: a journaled `RegisterCheckpoint` control record (legs = []) naming the watermark and the fold digest per register family; verify-by-fold runs from the last checkpoint or from genesis on demand; the checkpoint cadence is an adaptive decision with a decision card and a pinned fallback (every N entries), per the adaptive-decision contract.
3. Recovery: `fa registers rebuild` discards every register vertex and refolds from genesis (or from a checkpoint whose digest verifies); the rebuilt cells equal the maintained ones (metamorphic `rebuild = maintained`); `fa verify registers` stays green across the rebuild.
4. Reads: the report paths use maintained cells only when their watermark covers the requested known-at and the cells' verify digest matches; otherwise they fold (never a stale answer; the envelope reports which path answered).
5. Switch-over rule: when the substrate's Ripple views land, the maintainer becomes the registered interim's replacement per Appendix H; the rule is recorded in foundation_dependencies.toml.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: after N posts, `advance` moves the watermark by N and the maintained trial balance equals the full fold byte-for-byte; a crash between fold and watermark move (fa-sim crash point) leaves cells that re-advance to the same result; `rebuild` reproduces every cell; [ ] planted negatives: a maintainer mutation that skips one entry class is caught by verify-by-fold; a checkpoint with a forged digest is refused on rebuild; reading maintained cells past their watermark is refused by the read path test; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-04 register-never-more-authoritative, live) + metamorphic; [ ] consumers: every report path, G1 register verification, fa-sim campaigns; [ ] no-claim boundary: incremental equality is proven on the covered register families only.

TESTS: fa-registers integration tests with watermark and digests logged, fa-sim crash-point campaign for the maintainer, metamorphic rebuild test, CLI binary tests.

title: Statistical audit lane with independent oracles: in-house exact Benford/KS/chi-square procedures checked against frankenscipy fsci-stats (test-only), NumPy-reproducible sampling via franken_numpy fnp-random-core (PCG64DXSM), property suites on frankensim fs-propcheck
description:
WHY: doctrine 12 — a detector's score is `statistical` evidence, never an invariant; an examiner must be able to re-run the numbers in Python. frankenscipy (/data/projects/frankenscipy) has chisquare, power_divergence, kstest/ks_1samp, binomtest and Binomial/Hypergeometric/Poisson/ChiSquared distributions — all f64, so it cannot produce the certified statistic but is an ideal TEST-ONLY checker (fa-lantern dev-dependency; 4 MB lib.rs compile cost noted). franken_numpy's fnp-random-core (366 lines, zero deps, forbid(unsafe)) gives SeedSequence + Pcg64Dxsm bit-compatible with np.random.PCG64DXSM, so a sample drawn from a declared seed is reproducible in Python; the seed is a declared input (no entropy capability, doctrine 3). frankensim's fs-propcheck (zero deps: deterministic property testing with shrinking and seed replay) and fs-rand (seeded streams independent of scheduling) serve the §16.6 property/metamorphic suites and fa-gen.
WHAT: (1) crates/fa-lantern first slice: exact-integer Benford first/second-digit expected counts (rational expectation × n, law-rounded), chi-square and KS statistics over register legs with a certificate; (2) `fa sample random|mus --seed <declared> --size n` over open items/legs using fnp-random-core, output reproducible by a documented NumPy snippet; (3) dev-dependencies: fsci-stats pinned by git rev as the differential oracle for the statistics (tolerance stated as an f64 oracle bound, never applied to amounts); fs-propcheck for property suites; (4) registry rows for the procedures' claim classes.
ACCEPTANCE: [ ] oracle differential passes on fixtures and generated histories; [ ] sample reproducibility test vectors (seed → indices) pinned; [ ] no float in any amount path; [ ] `fa capabilities --json` lists the procedures with claim class statistical. UPSTREAM: frankenscipy — integer/exact-rational entry points for expected counts, or document f64 as oracle-only.
notes:
Upstream issue filed 2026-10-10: https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/frankenscipy/issues/16 (oracle numerical contract; exact entry points; split lib.rs).
TESTING (idea-wizard pass 1): every slice lands unit tests in the owning crate AND an end-to-end script-level test (binary test in crates/fa-cli/tests/cli.rs where a verb is involved) with detailed, greppable logging of inputs, digests, and verdicts; external tools absent => UNRUN, never a fake pass; gate stays rch-only.

title: fa-intents first slice: typed intents with canonical bytes, Book::plan dry-run returning a Plan with a PlanCertificate, Book::commit(plan) re-validating the bound fields (PlanInvalidated refusals), confirm_plan gating, non-null certificate in the robot envelope
description:
WHY (reality check 2026-10-10, CobaltGull): Bet A6 says agents work through typed intents with dry-run plans, and plan §19 says the Genesis slice takes "real PostEntry, IntentHeader and Plan types from fa-intents". At 96d1918 `fa::Book` has `post` but no `session/plan/commit`; `plan_certificate` is always `None` (fa-cli main.rs ~1750, fa book.rs ~849); the robot envelope's `certificate` field is emitted as `null`; `confirm_plan` has zero hits. An Agent-profile capability is refused on trunk with a pointer to drafts (fa-s7x), so today an agent cannot post at all. Intents are the laws-layer abstraction (crate layer "laws": pure, stripped Cx) that both drafts (fa-s7x) and Canon (W6) build on, so this slice must exist before either.

WHAT (first real slice, not a prototype):
1. `crates/fa-intents` (laws layer; no I/O, no Cx with capabilities): `IntentHeader { book, branch, principal, capability_ref, idempotency_key, known_at? }`, the intent union for the classes the kernel admits today (PostEntry, Reverse, Reserve, Resolve, Settle, PeriodTransition, DocumentAdd) with Appendix B field names, a canonical byte form (versioned, additive-minor, tag-coded like fa:entry:v1) and `proposal_digest` (which already exists in the kernel; move the single source here).
2. `Book::plan(&cap, intent) -> Plan`: a dry run that runs the full posting pipeline up to but excluding commit (admission, period law, evidence minimum, balance law, limits, SoD) against a snapshot, returning the effects (legs, mirrors it would move, approvals it needs, refusal it would raise) and a `PlanCertificate { proposal_digest, effects_commitment, snapshot_seq, security_policy_epoch, expires_at_seq }`; nothing is written.
3. `Book::commit(&cap, plan)`: re-validates the certificate's bound fields (plan §4.6 line 371: proposal digest, effects commitment, coordinate, policy epoch, current SoD, execution authority) inside the serializable transaction and refuses `PlanInvalidated { reason }` (new FA-REF codes with catalog rows) when any changed; otherwise commits with `plan_certificate` recorded on the entry and emitted in the robot envelope (`certificate` non-null).
4. `confirm_plan`: dangerous verbs (post with post_closed, period close/lock/reopen, resolve voids) require `--yes` or a `--confirm-plan <certificate>` whose digest matches; the refusal names the safe alternative (`--dry-run`).
5. CLI: `fa post --dry-run` emits the plan with its certificate (Agent-profile capabilities imply dry-run once per session, §15); `fa commit --plan <file|digest>`; robot events `plan`, `plan_invalidated`.
6. Oracle: fa-reference models plan = pure evaluation and commit = re-evaluation under the current state; differential plants: a plan invalidated by a concurrent close, by an epoch change, by a revoked capability, by changed legs; a valid plan commits byte-identically to a direct post.

ACCEPTANCE: [ ] positive: `fa post --dry-run --json` returns a certificate and writes nothing (journal head unchanged, proven by `fa verify registers` and an entry count); the same plan committed produces the same entry bytes as a direct post (metamorphic test); [ ] planted negatives: each `PlanInvalidated` reason is exercised by a test that changes exactly that bound field between plan and commit; [ ] proof class: invariant (FA-INV-11.core: certificates replayable) + differential; [ ] consumers: fa-s7x drafts (intent-log), fa-canon (intents bound to rule families), fa-cli/fa-mcp dry-run macros, FA-INV-11; [ ] no-claim boundary: a certificate proves what the plan bound, not that the intent was economically correct.

title: Resolve special periods, carry-forward folds, and report cutoffs
description:
References: §§4.8, 7.1-7.5, 8.6, 12.1/12.5, 15.6, Appendix A/C/F (lines 349, 475-491, 552, 717, 733, 919, 1181, 1265-1279, 1330).
A date must resolve to exactly one Period, but normal December, adjustment period 13 and closing/opening periods can share civil dates. There is no target-period field on Entry/PostEntry or registered routing rule to disambiguate. Shared calendar identity also needs separation from per-book period state.
The fold boundary is not defined for stock vs flow: FOR PERIOD filters effective dates, while balance-sheet/TB positions require opening balances; §7.5 additionally posts next-year opening balances despite an all-time append-only fold. Simple cash 100 at year end plus a new opening 100 becomes 200 under All unless openings are anchors or an explicit selection law excludes double counting. Closing entries likewise must not zero the income-statement activity reported for the closed year.
§8.6 imports opening trial balance plus optional full legacy history; specify a cut so both cannot be counted twice.
§7.4 defines originally reported as first Closed, while close can include further adjusting entries before publication/lock. Either label this view as first close or persist a ReportPublication fact/certificate; retain AS REPORTED IN for actual filings.
Required examples: Dec 31 normal/adjustment/closing, FY aggregate, Jan opening, pre/post-close P&L and BS, known-at retrospective correction, multi-book shared calendar with independent status, migration opening+detail. Special-period reference: https://help.sap.com/docs/SAP_S4HANA_ON-PREMISE/651d8af3ea974ad1a4d74449122c620e/2252d7531a4d424de10000000a174cb4.html . W1/W3/W7/W9, G0.
Appendix C refuses PriorPeriodAdjustment in Open/SoftClosed, although §8.1 defines it as an opening-retained-earnings adjustment. Decide whether it posts into the current open period while referring to historical error periods, or whether its class name means a different operation; do not force a current-period correction into a closed/locked target.

title: substrate: fgdb-sim FaultFile::sync_dirents retires namespace debts BEFORE the fallible backing open/sync_all returns (vfs.rs ~1313) — a failed or cancelled barrier can leave an unfenced name retained across a simulated crash; upstream fix with per-op identities captured before the first await and same-generation retirement after the real barrier
description: WHY (WhiteCreek 3706 / GoldenHollow 3621, 2026-10-11, source review of fgdb-sim at the pinned rev and the private alias candidate a3a636bd): FaultFile::sync_dirents removes the directory's namespace debts and only then awaits the backing open + sync_all. If the backing call fails or the future is cancelled, the debts are already gone, so a later simulated crash wrongly retains the unfenced name; the simulator then certifies durability the real filesystem would not give. Moving the removal after the await alone is also wrong: a concurrent operation that adds a new debt between the capture and the retirement would be cleared by the older barrier. This is separate from the alias/absolute-path repair in fa-n4m and must not be conflated with it. Doctrine 10: fixed upstream in frankengraphdb, never patched here. WHAT (design from 3706): (1) capture stable per-op debt identities (e.g. an Arc token compared by ptr_eq, or a generation number) under the lock BEFORE the first await, preserving the empty-debt and lie-trigger behaviours; (2) await the real backing barrier; (3) under the lock again, retire only the captured same-generation debts; an Err or a cancellation leaves every debt in place; an older generation's barrier cannot retire a newer debt. (4) Upstream PR with probes, then the joint fgdb/fgdb-sim re-pin here (franken-stack.lock), then re-run every FaultVfs regression. ACCEPTANCE (probes, all upstream): [ ] backing reopen/sync failure preserves the debt and a crash loses the name; [ ] retry success survives the crash; [ ] pause after the real backing sync, add debt B, resume: A survives, B is lost; [ ] a second barrier that retires A before B defeats index reuse (identity, not position); [ ] a dropped paused future retains its debt; [ ] proof class: bounded_model (simulation) — no broader crash certification; [ ] consumers: fa-txf FaultVfs regression, fa-0fl crash campaign, fa-n4m re-pin; [ ] no-claim boundary: this makes the simulator honest about failed barriers; it says nothing new about the host filesystem. Deletion condition: closes when the upstream fix is re-pinned and the probes are live.
